result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, so the plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/` and `mock-größe/` cases are covered. I haven't tested the new rule against any of these paths, including the elasticsearch one. The existing `*Scoping*` tests in `codeanalyzer` pass, but they don't check the new cases.

In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, I changed the two mock patterns from `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+` to `[^/\\]*`. The folder name can now be anything except a path separator, including nothing at all.

- **Backslash paths:** these already worked, because the filter normalizes separators before matching. I excluded `\` from the name so a match can't run across a Windows-style separator.
- **Other matches:** folders like `remock/` and `demo/` still don't match, since the name must start with `mock`. Neither do files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java`, because the pattern requires a `/` right after the folder name.
- **Existing folders:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still match, because the new pattern allows everything the old one did.
- **Relative paths:** like the old pattern, this one needs a `/` before the folder name. A path that begins directly with `mock/` and has nothing before it still isn't caught.

I didn't commit anything.
